small_guidance:
- The fused post-conv kernel is already at ~1.01x of baseline; the conv (Conv2d 8→32, k=3, 128×256×256) now dominates. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on the groupnorm kernel will not move the needle — focus must shift to the conv.
- If keeping the current structure, try BLOCK_SIZE=2048 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=2, and precompute c_global broadcast once per block instead of in both passes; also cache (x+b)*s sigmoid by storing to a scratch buffer between passes to avoid recomputing sigmoid in pass 2.
- Load bias/scale/gn_weight/gn_bias once per channel (CHANNELS_PER_GROUP is 4, tiny) into registers outside the HW loop instead of gathering per-element via `c_global` indexing.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output spatial tile), with BLOCK_M≈OC(32), BLOCK_N≈64-128 over output HW, BLOCK_K=IC*kh*kw=72. Fold the post-conv bias add, scale multiply, and sigmoid into its epilogue so only one tensor write happens before GroupNorm.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout end-to-end so the K reduction (IC × kh × kw) is contiguous and the OC dimension coalesces across warps; this also makes the subsequent GroupNorm reduction over (HW, C/group) friendlier.
- Consider a two-kernel pipeline: (1) conv+bias+scale+sigmoid writing NHWC fp32, (2) GroupNorm reading NHWC with one program per (N, group) doing a two-pass Welford. Do NOT fuse GN into the conv (output spatial reduction crosses tiles), but ensure the intermediate is laid out so GN loads coalesce.
